items.title: Russell takes crushing pole as Antonelli crashes out in Q1; Sainz and Perez both hit with grid penalties
items.summary: George Russell claimed his fifth pole of 2026 by 0.837s over Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri, describing it as "the perfect lap". His Mercedes team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli struck the Turn 1 wall early in Q1, breaking his suspension and ending his session; he will start 16th. Max Verstappen, fastest in FP3, could only manage eighth after a session he called "not good enough". Two grid penalties followed: Carlos Sainz drops from P9 to P14 (five places) for failing to slow for yellow flags across two marshalling sectors in Q3, plus two penalty points; Sergio Perez drops three places for impeding Piastri in Q1, but keeps P20 because Alonso and Stroll's larger engine-component penalties fall behind him.
items.why_it_matters: Antonelli's crash removes the championship leader from a realistic points-scoring grid slot in a season he already trails Russell in the standings fight, while Sainz's penalty costs Williams what would have been its best grid position of the year on a heavily-upgraded car. Combined with Alonso's now-30-place and Stroll's 20-place penalties, the grid order will differ substantially from the raw qualifying classification.

items.title: Alonso's grid penalty grows to 30 places after a fourth exceeded PU element in FP3
items.summary: The Technical Delegate's Document 33 (25 September, 12:43) reports Aston Martin fitted Fernando Alonso's car with a new energy store unit during FP3 — his 7th of the 3 allowed for the season, a fourth element over his allocation for this event. The Stewards' Document 34 imposes a further 5-place grid penalty on top of the already-confirmed 25-place Document 20 ruling, taking Alonso's cumulative grid penalty for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix to 30 places. Lance Stroll's separately confirmed 20-place penalty (Document 21) for exceeding his own allocation is unchanged. Elsewhere, the Stewards ruled (Document 19) that Valtteri Bottas's FP1 overtake of Albon under a yellow flag warranted no penalty, and the Turn 19 FP2 impeding investigation (Documents 22–23, summonses for Hamilton and Lawson) is resolved: Document 29 gives Lewis Hamilton (Car 44) a driving reprimand for impeding Liam Lawson's Car 30, with no separate ruling published against Lawson's own summons.
items.why_it_matters: A 30-place penalty exceeds the entire field, so Alonso will start last regardless of his qualifying position — removing any incentive to push for grid position in Qualifying and reshaping how Aston Martin approaches the session and the race strategy that follows. The Bottas ruling also sets a practical precedent for how tightly-timed yellow-flag overtakes are judged this weekend.

items.title: Hadjar returns to Red Bull for Baku after signing a 2027 extension
items.summary: Hadjar returns after missing Zandvoort, Monza and Madrid with a wrist fracture and has renewed with Red Bull for 2027. He says the simulator test went well but expects some continuing pain. Lawson returns to Racing Bulls and Tsunoda reverts to reserve.
items.why_it_matters: Baku's confirmed Red Bull/Racing Bulls line-up is the regular Verstappen-Hadjar pairing plus Lawson at Racing Bulls; do not carry the previous replacement chain into session results or teammate comparisons.

items.title: Williams brings its long-awaited FW48 upgrade package to Baku
items.summary: Formula1.com and The Race report that Williams is bringing its delayed FW48 package to Azerbaijan. Vowles told Formula1.com after Friday practice that it is 'a step in the right direction but not enough'; Albon and Sainz had earlier cautioned it may not deliver the full gain calculated months ago while the midfield continued to develop.
items.why_it_matters: This is a round-specific upgrade now tested in real practice conditions, not just a pre-weekend expectation — the team's own post-FP2 verdict tempers the pre-race optimism.
